subject: Maths
title: Gradient and y-intercept
subtitle: Straight-Line Graphs · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate the gradient of a line and identify the y-intercept from a graph or coordinates.

key_vocab.definition: The gradient measures how steep a line is: rise ÷ run. A positive gradient slopes upward; a negative gradient slopes downward.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate the gradient of a line and identify the y-intercept from a graph or coordinates.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: gradient -- The gradient measures how steep a line is: rise ÷ run. A positive gradient slopes upward; a negative gradient slopes downward.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Gradient = change in y divided by change in x. Pick any two points on the line.
m = y₂ - y₁ ÷ x₂ - x₁
Rise over run

Key examples:
  ✓ Gradient = (y₂ - y₁) ÷ (x₂ - x₁)  (rise over run)
  ✓ Points (1, 3) and (4, 9): m = 6 ÷ 3 = 2  (change in y over change in x)
  ✓ Horizontal line has gradient 0  (no rise)
  ✗ Gradient = run ÷ rise  (it is rise ÷ run)
  ✗ Vertical line has gradient 0  (it is undefined)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – from two points
  Find the gradient of the line through (2, 3) and (5, 9).
  Rise = 9 - 3 = 6
  Run = 5 - 2 = 3
  Gradient = 6 ÷ 3 = 2
  m = 2
  (Subtract y-values for rise, x-values for run.)

Example 2 – negative gradient
  Find the gradient of the line through (1, 7) and (4, 1).
  Rise = 1 - 7 = -6
  Run = 4 - 1 = 3
  Gradient = -6 ÷ 3 = -2
  m = -2
  (A negative answer means the line slopes downward.)

sections.title: Gradient from two points
sections.content:
Calculate the gradient.

(a) (1, 2) and (3, 8)
(b) (0, 5) and (4, 13)
(c) (2, 6) and (5, 6)
(d) (1, 10) and (3, 4)

sections.title: Positive and negative gradients
sections.content:
Find the gradient and state whether it slopes up or down.

(a) (0, 0) and (4, 12)
(b) (2, 9) and (5, 3)
(c) (-1, 4) and (3, 12)
(d) (0, 7) and (7, 0)

sections.title: Fractional gradients
sections.content:
Calculate the gradient. Leave as a fraction if needed.

(a) (0, 1) and (4, 3)
(b) (2, 5) and (8, 7)
(c) (0, 6) and (3, 4)
(d) (1, 2) and (5, 5)

sections.title: Finding the y-intercept
sections.content:
Find the y-intercept using y = mx + c.

(a) m = 2, passes through (3, 10)
(b) m = -1, passes through (4, 1)
(c) m = 3, passes through (2, 11)
(d) m = &frac{1}{2}, passes through (6, 7)

sections.title: Mixed gradient problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Find m and c for the line through (0, -3) and (2, 1)
(b) Line with m = -2 through (1, 5). Find c.
(c) Points (3, 4) and (6, 4). Describe the line.
(d) Is gradient (4-1)/(2-5) positive or negative?
(e) Line through (-2, -3) and (4, 9). Find equation.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Gradient = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)
✗ Gradient = change in x over change in y
✓ A negative gradient means the line slopes downward left to right
✗ A vertical line has gradient zero
✓ The y-intercept is found by substituting x = 0

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Gradient from two points:
  (a) m = 3
  (b) m = 2
  (c) m = 0
  (d) m = -3

Positive and negative gradients:
  (a) m = 3, slopes up
  (b) m = -2, slopes down
  (c) m = 2, slopes up
  (d) m = -1, slopes down

Fractional gradients:
  (a) m = &frac{1}{2}
  (b) m = &frac{1}{3}
  (c) m = -&frac{2}{3}
  (d) m = &frac{3}{4}

Finding the y-intercept:
  (a) c = 4
  (b) c = 5
  (c) c = 5
  (d) c = 4

Mixed gradient problems:
  (a) m = 2, c = -3
  (b) c = 7
  (c) Horizontal, m = 0, c = 4
  (d) Negative (= -1)
  (e) y = 2x + 1
